title: Danab Commandos Launch Planned Sweep on Al-Shabaab Movements in Lower Shabelle's Madax-Maroodi Area
detail: Somalia's elite Danab Special Forces carried out a planned operation on September 7, 2026 in the Madax-Maroodi area of Lower Shabelle region after receiving intelligence on Al-Shabaab fighters' movements there, Shabelle Media Network reported. The military said the aim was to disrupt the group's movements and prevent it from establishing bases to plan and launch attacks, weakening its capabilities and improving security for local communities. No casualty figures or captures were disclosed, and the report has not yet been independently corroborated by other outlets.

media.caption: Danab commandos conducted a sweep against Al-Shabaab movements in Lower Shabelle's Madax-Maroodi area, Sep 7, 2026

title: Karachi Police Briefly Detain Family Members Protesting 140-Day Captivity of Pakistani Sailors Held by Somali Pirates
detail: Relatives of the 10 Pakistani crew members of the Palau-flagged tanker MT Honour 25 — hijacked off Somalia's Puntland coast on April 21, 2026 and still held after roughly 140 days — staged an overnight sit-in at Karachi's Sharea Faisal outside the Foreign Affairs ministry liaison office on September 6-7, 2026, warning they would begin a hunger strike if the government failed to secure the crew's release. Police briefly detained seven protesters early Monday morning, September 7, taking them to Tipu Sultan police station; families said officers were not initially allowing them to see the detainees, while police said the detentions followed use of loudspeakers without authorization and that protesters were dispersed without force — an account families disputed. Pakistan's Foreign Office said it remains 'actively engaged' in securing the crew's release; a legal advisor cited unspecified 'recent developments' in the case, including pirates reportedly lowering their ransom demand from the roughly $3 million previously sought. No ransom has been paid and no hostages released as of September 7.

media.caption: Karachi police briefly detained relatives of Pakistani sailors held by Somali pirates aboard MT Honour 25, Sep 7, 2026

title: Egyptian FM Warns Against 'Unilateral Measures' Threatening Somali Sovereignty, Presses for Egyptian Sailors' Release
detail: Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty met Somali counterpart Abdisalam Abdi Ali on the sidelines of the 166th Arab League Council ministerial session in Cairo on September 7, 2026, praising the 'significant development' in bilateral ties while warning against 'unilateral measures that could compromise or diminish' Somalia's sovereignty and reaffirming Egypt's support for its unity and territorial integrity. Abdelatty also raised Egypt's participation in AUSSOM and pressed Somali authorities to expedite the release of Egyptian sailors currently detained off Somalia's coast, calling for continued Somali government involvement in securing captives' freedom. The two ministers also discussed deepening economic, development and investment cooperation.

media.caption: Egyptian FM Badr Abdelatty met Somali FM Abdisalam Abdi Ali at the Arab League Council session in Cairo, Sep 7, 2026

title: Somali Journalist Bashir Mohamed Abdullahi Dies From Gunshot Wounds Sustained Covering Baidoa Clashes
detail: Bashir Mohamed Abdullahi, 23, a reporter for Arlaadi Media Network, died in the early hours of September 7, 2026 from gunshot wounds sustained on September 3 while covering fighting between federal forces and Laftagareen-aligned militia in Baidoa's Al Axmaar district. Armed men in uniform with covered faces stopped him, questioned him about his employer, and shot him twice in the back after he identified himself as a journalist. He underwent emergency surgery at Bay General Hospital but died before he could be transferred to Mogadishu for further treatment. The National Union of Somali Journalists (NUSOJ) and the International Federation of Journalists demanded a full investigation and accountability, calling it the second journalist killed in Somalia in 2026 and warning that chronic impunity for attacks on the press must end.

media.caption: NUSOJ demands justice after journalist Bashir Mohamed Abdullahi died of wounds sustained covering the Sep 3 Baidoa clashes

title: Bodies of Somali Al-Shabaab Fighters Found Among Houthi Casualties on Yemen's West Coast
detail: Yemen's anti-Houthi National Resistance Forces (NRF), led by Tareq Saleh and aligned with Yemen's internationally recognized government, said on September 7, 2026 that it found the bodies of Somali Al-Shabaab fighters among Houthi casualties from recent clashes on Yemen's west coast, identified through documents and personal belongings. The NRF said the discovery 'indicates co-ordination between the Iran-backed militia and armed groups across the region' — the second such reported discovery of Al-Shabaab operatives fighting alongside Houthi forces in Yemen. The claim has not been independently verified. It follows earlier reporting that Al-Shabaab opened communications with the Houthis in 2024 seeking anti-aircraft weapons, drones and shoulder-fired rockets, and that more than 100 Al-Shabaab fighters have travelled to Yemen for Houthi-run training, deepening concerns over an emerging Horn of Africa-Red Sea militant nexus.

media.caption: Yemen's National Resistance Forces say Somali Al-Shabaab fighters were found dead among Houthi casualties, Sep 7, 2026
